title: FuneralDesk: family portal, approvals and AI-drafted notices for independent UK funeral directors
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: Independent funeral directors spend hours on the phone collecting family details, choices and approvals, then writing notices and service sheets. FuneralDesk gives families a gentle online form and approval page and drafts the obituary, notices and order of service, without replacing the firm's main system.
hook: "Every family needs the same 40 details from us, at the worst moment of their life, and we take them over five phone calls."
story:
**Margaret runs a family-owned funeral home in Fife** with 7 staff and about **180 funerals a year**. For each one, her team collects the same details over several calls: names, dates, music, readings, flowers, newspaper notice wording, and written approval of the price estimate. Notices and service sheets are typed by hand, and errors in a name or date cause real hurt.

Scotland's statutory **Code of Practice for funeral directors** also expects clear prices, written estimates and good records. Margaret's case-management software handles bookings and invoices but not the back-and-forth with families. She wants a calm, simple page for families to fill in at their own pace, one-click approvals, and drafts she only needs to check.
whyNow: Scotland's Funeral Director Code of Practice, approved by the Scottish Parliament in January 2024, is statutory, and a licensing scheme and inspection regime are planned. Expectations on written estimates and records are rising across the UK.
evidence: Scotland's Funeral Director Code of Practice was approved by the Scottish Parliament on 31 January 2024 under the Burial and Cremation (Scotland) Act 2016, with a grace period to comply [Scottish Government]
The code applies to all funeral directors working in Scotland, wherever the business is based, ahead of a planned licensing scheme [Scottish Government impact assessment]

Funeral software prices range widely: Osiris about $100/month, Halcyon about 295/month, Parting Pro $469/month, and per-funeral pricing from about £5 (aggregator listings) [Software Advice / Capterra]
The only revenue evidence for a funeral add-on is one unverified anecdote of $29k MRR at $650 per location, sold via association newsletters [Medium via Top 25 report]

whyReal.title: Repetitive, emotional admin
whyReal.text: The same details are collected for every funeral, by phone, from grieving families. Mistakes hurt.

whyReal.title: Rules push for written records
whyReal.text: Scotland's statutory code expects clear estimates and records, and UK-wide regulation is being discussed.

whyReal.title: Closed, reachable community
whyReal.text: Independent funeral directors are listed in association directories and read association newsletters.

whyReal.title: Honest weakness

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Independent funeral directors with 1–5 branches and 80–800 funerals a year.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The owner or senior funeral director.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: Scotland and the rest of the UK, then Ireland and Australia.

solution.title: Gentle family page
solution.text: the funeral director sends one link; family members fill in details, choices and memories at their own pace, from any phone.

solution.title: Estimate and approvals
solution.text: the written price estimate and key choices are shown clearly and approved with one tap, with a dated record.

solution.title: AI drafts
solution.text: obituary, newspaper and online notices, and the order of service are drafted from the family's answers, for staff to edit.

solution.title: Checklist per funeral
solution.text: a simple task list (registrar, crematorium, flowers, music) with who does what.

solution.title: Records
solution.text: everything is stored per funeral, ready if a regulator or family asks.

must: Written estimate display and approval with timestamp
later: Integration with UK funeral case-management systems
Price-list page that follows UK rules

risks.answer: Sell through association newsletters and peer referrals; offer to set up the first funerals by hand.
Staff always edit AI drafts; careful wording; strict data handling.

risks.answer: Do not build until 2 letters of intent at £99+ per month.

questions: Walk me through the first 48 hours after a family calls you.

Who writes notices and orders of service today, and how long does it take?
What software do you pay for, and what is missing?
Would you pay £99 a month to save 2–3 hours per funeral?
